messages:
alex: heads up — after flipping continuous-batching=true on staging we saw a weird drop in prefix cache hit-rate and an increase in tail latency. quick summary: hit-rate went from ~38% -> ~21% over a 30m window, P99 latency +12%. :eyes:

maria: ugh. do you have the breakdown by batch size and model? could be that mixing small/large seqs hurts cache locality.

alex: digging now. quick prom query I used:```promql
sum by(model) (increase(prefix_cache_hits_total[30m])) / sum by(model) (increase(prefix_cache_requests_total[30m])) * 100
```results attached in dashboard -> model-a most impacted, model-b stable. batch size distribution shifted: more heterogeneous batches (mix of 1-8 tokens and 200-400 tokens) after the change.

sanjay: that matches my microprofile runs. continuous batching merges requests across different prefixes which reduces per-batch prefix repetition. fewer repeats => fewer cache hits and more KV loads. I ran a quick trace showing KV cache miss rate rises with batch diversity. snippet from the profiler:```text
batch_id=0x7fae, composition=[p1,p2,p3,p_long], kv_cache_hits=1, kv_cache_misses=3
```

elaine: two axes to consider: 1) cache keying (are we keying on full prompt string or prefix hash + length bucket?), 2) warmup. Right now key = sha256(prefix) + model_rev. That means slightly different prefix whitespace or tokens create different keys. If batch mixing increases partial overlaps, we lose hits.

maria: can we try bucketing keys by canonicalized prefix up to N tokens? e.g. key := sha256(normalize(prefix_trimmed_to_64_tokens)) + model_rev. tradeoff: coarser keys might increase false positive hits (bad) but could help hit-rate. Need quality eval.

alex: also noticed warmup behavior: previously long-lived sessions warmed the KV cache because many similar prefixes arrived sequentially. continuous batching interleaves other traffic so warmup windows get broken. Potential fix: targeted async pre-warm for hot prefixes on model load / after rollouts — prefetch top-K prefixes from recent telemetry.

sanjay: i simulated pre-warm of top-500 prefixes on model pod start. net effect: hit-rate +7ppt and P95 latency improved ~4%. but cold-start memory pressure increases ~30MB on the GPU process.

elaine: memory looks fine for Dedicated but not for constrained Private deployments. We should make pre-warm tunable by deployment profile. Also consider incremental warmup: pre-warm only prefixes above threshold QPS.

maria: another idea — change batching heuristic to prefer grouping by prefix fingerprint when possible, as an optional constraint. e.g. batcher: try to form batches with prefix_fingerprint affinity up to Xms window, then fallback to throughput mode. That gives a knob between latency and hit-rate.

alex: agreed. we can A/B a flag: `batcher.affinity.prefix=true|false` and measure both end-to-end latency and cache hit-rate. simple perf test plan: 1) baseline continuous-batching on, affinity off 2) affinity on 10ms window 3) affinity on 50ms window. collect: prefix_hit_rate, p95/p99, tokens/sec.

sanjay: i'll add a microbenchmark that replays a corpus with realistic prefix skew to the perf harness. script: `./scripts/replay-corpus --corpus=prod-sample --affinity-window=50` and I'll push results to the perf dashboard.

ci-bot: perf job queued: https://ci.redwood/pipelines/1799345610 -> results in ~15m :robot_face:

elaine: quick note on keying experiments — if we bucket keys by prefix-length, include model_rev and quantization bits. Quantization can change embeddings so key mismatch possible across quantized variants. keep that in mind for Dedicated/private heterogeneous fleets.

maria: also need eval harness: run quality/regression checks on outputs when using coarser keying or pre-warm. we can't trade correctness for hit-rate. i'll draft a prompt-set and loss metric.

alex: action items: 
- sanjay: run replay with affinity=10/50/0 and pre-warm toggles, upload perf.csv by EOD.
- elaine: prototype prefix-bucketing key function (normalize + trim) and estimate false-positive QPS impact.
- maria: prepare eval prompts and threshold for quality regression.
- me: flip canary with `batcher.affinity.prefix=true` on a small Dedicated pool once we have microbench numbers.

maria: thanks. one more ask — instrument batch composition telemetry: emit `batch.prefix_entropy` and `batch.unique_prefix_count` per batch so we can correlate hit-rate to composition. small change, big visibility.

alex: +1. adding that to the PR. will also add the PromQL for quick dashboards:```promql
sum(rate(batch_unique_prefix_count[5m])) by(model)
sum(rate(prefix_cache_miss_total[5m])) by(model)
```

sanjay: 👍 i'll watch the job and iterate on the script if we see anomalies.

elaine: I'll sketch a rollout plan for Dedicated vs Private (tunable pre-warm and affinity windows).

alex: great. thanks all. we'll reconvene after the perf run. :thumbsup:
